newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ ends weaker on surprise USDA Fla box count.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ ends weaker on surprise USDA Fla box count.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures closed weaker but off the lows, pressured by technically-driven selling and U.S. Department of Agriculture data released before the open, dealers said.
May juice ended 3.45 weaker at 81.55 cents per pound, having ranged from 82.75 to 79.50 cents. The back months settled 3.30 to 1.70 cents lower.
Volume was estimated at 5,000 lots compared with Monday's official 2,687 lots.
The USDA raised its forecast of Florida's orange crop to a record 222 million 90-lb boxes from 220 million boxes. Early and mid-season oranges are expected to reach a record 135 million boxes.
Yield remained unchanged at 1.54 gallons per box.

"People were shocked by the last report when the estimate was unchanged at 220 (million boxes) and they expected a downward revision in this report," Bernard Savaiko, an analyst with PaineWebber, said.
"When that failed to materialize there was shock in the marketplace."
Monday's close under support and the 40-day moving average of 85.30 cents in May added technical pressure to the selloff, analysts said.
Additionally, NYCE's speculator/hedge report showed the speculators to be holding a 70.1 percent net long position.
"The specs are long the market and when they start bailing out we're going to see a big selloff," an analyst said.
Support was pegged at 77.50 and then at 65.45 in May.
